items.title: Michael Moore interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997
items.q: It’s like the George Steinbrenner way of running a baseball team.

ctx.x: It’s interesting, even tonight it looks like they have a set-up where the people are going to be eating dinner during the first significant portion of this party. These jazz parties are an interesting kind of phenomenon. Do you enjoy making the circuit on these things?

I do. I’ve been doing them now for I guess I started doing them back in the mid 70s I think. So I’ve been doing them a long time. I actually enjoy some more than others, depending on the circumstances. The thing that I don’t like about them is the fact that they’re big jam sessions, and the lack of organization that goes on, because of the nature of the beast. I mean it’s a phenomenon that in a way has taken the place of a lot of clubs and things of yesteryear that are no longer in existence. And I’m grateful for…
Maybe some kind of balance would be nice, if they had a band during part of the evening and then did the more traditional format.
